title: Naturality of the canonical presheaf-to-sheaf tensor map
statement: Let (C,J) be a site and R a sheaf of commutative rings. Let A,Aprime,B,Bprime be sheaves of R-modules, f:Aprime -> A and g:Bprime -> B. Write s(A,B) for homTensorSectionMap [lem-sc-hom-tensor-degreewise], the unit of module sheafification [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification] followed by the underlying inverse of the sheaf tensor comparison [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. Then s(Aprime,Bprime);(f tensor g).val = (f.val tensor g.val);s(A,B), an equality of presheaf module morphisms. No invertibility of f or g, boundedness, or hypothesis on sections is imposed.

source.place: Section 03EK (tensor product as sheafification), and Lemma 03CY (module sheafification universal property); https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/03EK and https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/03CY

proof.text: Write S for module sheafification, eta for its unit, epsilon for its counit, and c(A,B) for tensorObjIsoSheafification. By definition c is the tensor of inverse counit components followed by the tensorator of S. Naturality of epsilon and of that tensorator gives (f tensor g);c(A,B) = c(Aprime,Bprime);S(f.val tensor g.val). This uses only the sheaf tensor construction, not monoidal closure.

Compose the preceding equality with the inverse comparison on the left and right. It becomes c(Aprime,Bprime) inverse;(f tensor g) = S(f.val tensor g.val);c(A,B) inverse. Apply the forgetful functor and precompose with eta at Aprime.val tensor Bprime.val. Naturality of eta moves f.val tensor g.val to the left of the unit at A.val tensor B.val. Associativity of composition gives the asserted equality, since s is precisely eta followed by c inverse. The argument also works for zero morphisms or zero modules and does not claim pure tensors globally generate a sheaf tensor.

proof_origin.place: Expanded naturality consequence of Section 03EK and Lemma 03CY, read online; the source comparison is implemented in WeilConjectures.Algebra.Category.ModuleCat.Sheaf.Monoidal.
